resolutions.researcher_notes: KOC's Wafra Joint Operations (WJO) to BS-171 gas export pipeline. Nov 2024 Gulf Construction Online reports CGC as lowest bidder (pre-award = proposed stage); April 2025 Zawya reports CGC won the EPC letter of award. CONTRADICTION FLAG: an EPC contract was awarded April 2025, so 'proposed' may be understated — arguably 'construction' or in-development. No source yet confirms construction start on the ground, so 'proposed'/pre-construction is defensible for now; worth a status review.

ProposalYear 2022 supported by Arab News (10 Jan 2022, Wayback of the original dead node/2001621, citing KUNA): Kuwait Gulf Oil Co. signed an initial agreement with Saudi Arabian Chevron to export spare gas from Wafra Joint Operations, with short- and long-term plans to build out gas export — the origin of this export line. Single strong primary (KUNA-sourced); no fully independent second confirming the 2022 proposal specifically, hence medium.

StartYear1 2028 is DERIVED, not stated. Sources give a 30-month completion period; Zawya reports the award announced 24 April 2025. 30 months from award ≈ late 2027 (~Oct 2027), not 2028. CONTRADICTION FLAG: 2028 slightly overstates the implied ~2027 completion; plausible only with commissioning slippage. No source states 2028 explicitly — tier low; recommend reconciling StartYear1 to 2027 or confirming a firmer schedule.

FuelSource 'Wafra Field' well supported: DMS Universe describes a 65 km gas export pipeline from Wafra Joint Operations (WJO) to BS-171; Arab News (Jan 2022) describes exporting spare/surplus gas from the Wafra Joint Operations area. Two independent origins agree the gas comes from Wafra.

SegmentCost $42,000,000 supported: both sources value CGC's WJO-to-booster-station gas pipeline EPC at KD12.7 million (~$42 million). Note the figure is the CGC EPC contract value (award ~2025), consistent with SegmentCostYear 2025 and SegmentCostUnits USD.

StartYear1=2028 supported. SICIM (contractor executing MGS III packages 10/14) states 'END OF WORK: 2028', client Saudi Aramco, Saudi Arabia. Blackridge project profile states construction commenced Q2 2024 and scheduled completion Q4 2028. Both independent, both confirm 2028 as the MGS III program end-of-work year. The specific EWPS-1-Shedgum EPC contract (Gas Arabian Services, signed 29 May 2024, 40-month duration) runs to ~2027-2028, consistent with the program-level Q4 2028 completion. Original Zawya current_ref is actually live (verified OK), but it gives contract duration not a start/completion year, so I cited the two sources that explicitly state 2028.

StartCountryOrArea=EndCountryOrArea=Saudi Arabia supported. Segment is the 56-inch east-west gas pipeline from EWPS-1 to Shedgum, both in Saudi Arabia's Eastern Province. MEED: 'Laying 56-inch east-west gas pipelines three and four from EWPS-1 to Shedgum, covering 56 km'; Zawya: 'Master Gas System expansion from SHEDGUM to EWPS-1'. Both confirm the route lies wholly within Saudi Arabia. SICIM (cited on Start) also lists it as Kingdom of Saudi Arabia.

VALUE CONTRADICTION FLAG. GEM SegmentCost=46,000,000 USD. The awarded EWPS-1-Shedgum EPC contract (Gas Arabian Services, signed 29 May 2024) is SAR 344,614,412 = ~92 million USD (Zawya, and Argaam: 'nearly SAR 344.6 million, excluding VAT', 40 months, 2024-2027 impact). Per MEED this package covers 'east-west gas pipelines three AND four from EWPS-1 to Shedgum' (two pipelines, 56 km). The GEM row is only pipeline '3' (EWPS-1-Shedgum "3"), so the 46,000,000 USD appears to be a GEM half-split of the ~92M USD contract across pipelines 3 and 4. No source states 46M for a single pipeline; the sources support ~92M USD / SAR 344.6M for the combined 3+4 package. Refs support the parent contract value; the exact 46M half is a GEM derivation. Recommend verifying whether the segment cost should instead be the full ~92M USD (SAR 344.6M) or remain the half-split, and whether pipeline 4 is a separate GEM row.

StartYear1=2028 = target completion/start-up of MGS Expansion Phase 3 (MGS-3), which the EWPS-1-Shedgum '4' segment belongs to. Blackridge explicitly states 'Project Completion Date: Q4 2028' and identifies Package 3 as laying 56-inch pipelines EWGP-3 and EWGP-4 from EWPS-1 to Shedgum (56km) in Eastern Province, Saudi Arabia, owned by Saudi Aramco. SPA (official Saudi Press Agency) and OGJ 25bn-contract-awards articles both independently reference the 2028 timeline for the strategic gas expansion. Three independent sources support 2028. Original Aramco press release (aramco.com/.../25bn-contract-awards) timed out on verification (ReadTimeout) so was dropped in favor of the SPA/OGJ reprints/originals of the same announcement.

StartCountryOrArea and EndCountryOrArea = Saudi Arabia. Both endpoints (Shedgum gas plant and EWPS-1) are in the Eastern Province of Saudi Arabia. Blackridge locates the project in 'Eastern Province of Saudi Arabia'; MEED describes the Shedgum-to-EWPS-1 Master Gas System expansion segments, all in Saudi Arabia. Two independent sources agree.

SegmentCost=$46,000,000 USD is an INFERRED per-pipeline half-split, not a directly stated figure. The Gas Arabian Services EPC contract for 'Master Gas System expansion from SHEDGUM to EWPS-1' is $92 million (SAR 344,614,412), covering two parallel 56-inch pipelines EWGP-3 and EWGP-4 (Blackridge: 'Lay 56-inch pipelines EWGP-3 and EWGP-4 from EWPS-1 to Shedgum'). This segment row is pipeline '4' only, so $92M / 2 = $46M. Zawya (from the Tadawul/Argaam disclosure) and MEED independently report the $92M Shedgum-EWPS-1 award. FLAG: the $46M is GEM's allocation of the shared two-pipe contract; no source states $46M for pipeline 4 alone. Tier medium because the underlying $92M contract is well-sourced but the split is an assumption.

StartYear1=2028 supported by two independent sources. Original Aramco press release (dead live URL, recovered via Wayback) verifies tokens '2028' and 'EWPS' for the MGS Phase 3 gas expansion. LengthKnown=150 km. Blackridge scope of work: 'Lay 56-inch diameter pipelines (EWGP-3 and EWGP-4) from EWPS-1 to EWPS-3 (300km)' — two parallel 56-inch lines totalling 300 km, i.e. ~150 km per line. This GEM row is line '3' (EWGP-3), so 150 km is the per-line figure derived from the paired 300 km stated for both lines. Single reference gives the length; 150 is an inference (300/2) rather than a directly stated per-line figure — flagging for reviewer. MEED/Aramco original was the prior dead ref; Aramco Wayback release confirms the segment but does not state a per-line km figure.
